doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

title: Starting trumpet after seeing Harry James, and first lessons
summary: Hal saw a Harry James movie in seventh grade, got a $40 cornet, and took summer lessons to win first chair in ninth grade in Riverside.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yes. I actually started when I was eleven. I went and saw a movie when I was in the seventh grade and it was Harry James, and he was the feature. He was the guy that was the focal point, and his band. And I remember Dick Haymes I think was in it and then a girl singer. And I went away wanting to play a trumpet because Harry was in front of the band playing. He won the singer away from I think Dick Haymes, whoever the other boy singer was. I went home and asked my dad, you know, if I could get a trumpet. So he went to a music store and got me a $40 cornet because it was cheaper. So I started in the seventh grade and brought it home and occasionally picked it up and practiced. And then when I was in the eighth grade my band director in junior high school — junior high school at that time was from seventh, eighth and ninth grade. So in the eighth grade, at the end of the eighth grade, the music director told me if I would take lessons from him over the summer he’d make me a first chair as a ninth grader. So I thought okay, I can do that. So I mowed lawns and got the $3 for a half hour lesson and I’d have to bicycle about 2-1/2 miles to his place and back. And I was first chair. So the high school — I’m from Riverside, California. I’m actually a sixth generation Californian. So when I got to be first chair, you know it’s fun because I was kind of a leader of a section.
